title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page sits among the 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' material: a Tannakian category over R, written M_R, with fundamental band/gerbe G. The neighbouring pages are unrelated: SGA 3 corrections, and an English translation of a Shafarevich-type embedding argument. The page begins with a corollary for 'the case of page 2'.

(1) Structure of the band. The identity part of the band splits as G^0 ≅ U^0 × G_m. The factor G_m is the weight (Tate) part, and ε = pr_2 is the weight character. An element j is defined as j(λ) = i_q(λ)^2, where i_q is presumably the weight/Tate cocharacter; j is a central 'sign/Weil' element.

(2) Tensor structure. The tensor-category structure of M_R is determined by two data: the band G, and the characteristic class of the gerbe in H^2(R,U).
- This class is the unique nonzero element of H^2(R, 2U).
- That element comes from the unique nonzero element of H^2(R,μ_2) = Br(R)_2 = Z/2, i.e. the class of the Hamilton quaternions.
- So the gerbe is non-neutral in the generic case. Equivalently, there is an object of degree (weight) 1 and rank 2 on which U^0 acts trivially. The tensor subcategory it generates is the 'R-twisted' form of Rep(G_m): the form twisted by the quaternion algebra, as for a supersingular elliptic curve, whose End⊗R = H.
- This matches the known phenomenon that motives over F_q are not neutral over R = Q_∞.

(3) The favourable case G_R ≠ ∅ (gerbe neutral over R).
- The set H^0(G_R) of isomorphism classes of R-fibre functors (R-points of the gerbe) is a torsor under H^1(R,U).
- For U an anisotropic (compact) torus, H^1(R,U) ≅ 2U(R) ≅ (Z/2)^{dim U}.
- To each R-point corresponds a 'structure polarisante' on G^0. This is a homomorphism i_1: μ_2 → G^0, probably over C (the image suggests G^0_C), with ε∘i_1 = id and i_1·ī_1 = j_R.
- The set Pol of such structures is also a torsor under 2U(R). The natural map H^0(G_R) → Pol(G_R) is 2U(R)-equivariant, hence bijective.
- In words: real fibre functors correspond exactly to polarising (Weil/Cartan-type) structures, i.e. to compact-form data.
- The page breaks off while beginning to discuss R-fibre functors.

Purpose. Classify the real Tannakian gerbe of motives (or of Weil-number / Hodge-type categories), its non-neutrality, and the relation between real fibre functors and polarisations. This is the archimedean part of a 'Galois theory of motives'.
errors: Cohomological identifications are stated without hypotheses. H^1(R,U) ≅ 2U(R) ≅ (Z/2)^{dim U} requires U to be an anisotropic (compact) torus, or at least needs the Tate-cohomology identification for the relevant U. This is not stated on the page.

There is a tension between saying the characteristic class is the nonzero element (so the gerbe is non-neutral) and then treating the 'favourable case' G_R ≠ ∅. Presumably these are two different situations, or the class lives in a quotient. It is unclear from the page alone.
Equivariance plus the torsor property gives bijectivity only once both sets are known to be nonempty. This holds in the favourable case, so the argument is fine there.

ideas.what: Band of the real motivic/Tannakian gerbe splits as U^0 × G_m with weight character ε
ideas.modern_name: Weight grading / weight cocharacter of the motivic Galois group; pro-torus for motives over finite fields (Weil-number torus)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne–Milne (1982), Milne (Motives over finite fields, 1994)

ideas.what: Characteristic class of the gerbe in H^2(R,U), coming from the quaternion class in H^2(R,μ_2); rank-2, weight-1 object generating the quaternion-twisted subcategory
ideas.modern_name: Non-neutrality of the Tannakian category of motives over F_q over R (supersingular elliptic curve, End⊗R = H)

ideas.what: R-points of the gerbe (real fibre functors up to iso) form a torsor under H^1(R,U) ≅ 2U(R)
ideas.modern_name: Classification of fibre functors by H^1 of the band (Giraud nonabelian cohomology)

ideas.what: Polarising structure i_1: μ_2 → G^0 with ε i_1 = id, i_1 ī_1 = j; bijection between real fibre functors and polarisations
ideas.modern_name: Polarisations of Tannakian categories over R, Weil/Cartan involutions, compact forms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (Ch. V, 1972); Deligne–Milne §5; Deligne (Kuga–Satake / Shimura varieties)

missed.claim: This is an early, Grothendieck-authored sketch linking real fibre functors of a motivic gerbe bijectively to 'polarising structures' (μ_2 → G^0 with conditions), each counted as a torsor under 2U(R). It predates or is contemporary with Saavedra's thesis treatment of polarisations, usually credited to Saavedra/Deligne.
missed.quote: L'application H^0(G_R) → Pol(G_R) est compatible avec les opérations de 2U(R), donc bijective.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's own role in the theory of polarisations and real gerbes of motives, later attributed to Saavedra and Deligne–Milne. It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page has substantive content on the real motivic gerbe: the quaternion characteristic class and the equivalence between polarisations and real fibre functors. The mathematics is known, from Saavedra, Deligne–Milne and Milne on motives over finite fields. The interest is historical attribution, not new results.
transcription_corrections: 'H^2(R, U_2)' is likely 'H^2(R, ₂U)' (2-torsion of U).
In 'μ_2 →^{i_1} G^0_R' the subscript in the image looks like ℂ (G^0_ℂ), consistent with the condition i_1 ī_1 = j_R involving complex conjugation.
'$H^0(G_R)$ est objet[?] isomorphe[?] de G_R' is probably 'H^0(G_R) ensemble des classes d'isomorphie d'objets de G_R ... est un torseur sous le groupe H^1(R,U)'.
'il existe une ... équivalence de M_R' is more likely 'il existe un objet de M_R de degré 1, rang 2'.
